title: The Quiet B
kidRule: B is a great hider! It stays quiet right after M, as in CLIMBER, and right before T, as in DOUBT. Its neighbor does all the talking!
hint: A quiet letter is hiding in this word. We do not say it, and it sits right next to an M or a T. Which letter is it?
reminder: A quiet B is hiding here: right after the M (M-B) or right before the T (B-T).

check.question: Why can't we hear the B in CLIMBER?
check.correctAnswer: B stays quiet when it comes right after M!
distractors: Because the letter I makes every B quiet
Because long words never say all of their letters

words.def: A person or animal that goes up things like rocks, trees, or mountains.
words.sent: The climber reached the top of the rocky wall.
words.story: A mountain goat is an amazing climber. Its hooves have soft, grippy pads that help it stand on tiny ledges!
words.card: The *climber* tried to *climb* a mountain of mashed potatoes!

words.def: To feel unsure that something is true.
words.sent: I doubt that my cat can really read.
words.story: Long ago this word was spelled without a B. Scholars added the B later to match the old Latin word 'dubitare', but nobody ever said it out loud!
words.card: I *doubt* the snail can finish a *doub*le scoop before it melts!

words.def: Not able to feel anything, like fingers that got very cold.
words.sent: My toes went numb after playing in the snow.
words.story: Your foot feels numb when you sit on it because the nerves get squished and stop sending messages for a while!
words.card: My toes went *numb*, so I ate a pea*nu*t butter sandwich to warm them up!

words.def: A person whose job is to fix water pipes, sinks, and toilets.
words.sent: The plumber fixed the dripping tap in the kitchen.
words.story: The word comes from the Latin name for the metal lead, because long ago water pipes were made of it!
words.card: The *plumber* found a purple *plum* stuck in the kitchen pipe!

words.def: Something, usually money, that you owe to someone.
words.sent: I paid my debt by giving back the two dollars I borrowed.
words.story: The B was put into this word hundreds of years ago to match the Latin word 'debitum', even though people kept saying it the old way!
words.card: *Deb* the duck paid her *debt* in bread crusts!

words.def: A room or building made of stone where someone was buried long ago.
words.sent: The explorers found golden treasure inside the ancient tomb.
words.story: The tomb of the Egyptian king Tutankhamun was found in 1922 with more than 5,000 treasures still inside!
words.card: The cat tiptoed in*to* the *tomb* and sneezed on a mummy!

words.def: An arm or a leg, or a big branch of a tree.
words.sent: The squirrel ran along the highest limb of the tree.
words.story: An octopus has eight limbs, and each one can taste what it touches!
words.card: The octopus waved every *limb* and said, 'Look, I can sw*im*!'

words.def: Not sure, or not likely to happen.
words.sent: It is doubtful that the snow will last until Friday.
words.story: Good scientists stay a little doubtful! They test an idea again and again before they believe it.
words.card: The snowman looked *doubtful*, and I *doubt* he liked the hot cocoa!

words.def: So small or gentle that it is hard to notice.
words.sent: The soup had a subtle taste of lemon.
words.story: Dogs can notice very subtle smells. A dog's sense of smell is at least 10,000 times stronger than a person's!
words.card: The *sub* sandwich had a *subtle* hint of sock, so I blamed the dog!

words.def: To give in to something because you cannot hold out any longer.
words.sent: I tried to stay awake, but I had to succumb to sleep.
words.story: Every animal has to succumb to sleep in the end! Dolphins solve this by resting only half of their brain at a time.
words.card: I had to *succumb* to a nap on a giant cu*cumb*er!
